prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so my recommendations are useful:
- When did the accident happen?
- Were you injured (minor, serious, hospitalized)?
- Have you already spoken with any insurance company or signed anything?
- Do you want local Pleasanton attorneys only, or are nearby cities (Dublin, Livermore, San Ramon, Walnut Creek) OK?

If you’d like, I can pull together a short list of personal-injury attorneys/firms in the Pleasanton area. If you prefer general guidance first, here’s how to choose the right lawyer and what to do now.

How to choose the right personal-injury (car-accident) lawyer
- Look for relevant experience: attorneys who focus on car accidents/personal injury and who have handled cases like yours (serious injury, soft-tissue, catastrophic, uninsured motorist, multi-vehicle).
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but you want a lawyer who will go to trial if the insurer won’t offer fair compensation.
- Track record and references: ask for past settlements/verdicts (not guarantees) and client references or online reviews.
- Communication: ask how you’ll be updated, who you’ll speak to (attorney or paralegal), and expected response times.
- Resources: serious cases may require private investigators, experts (medical, accident reconstruction), and funds to advance costs — confirm the firm can cover those.
- Fee structure: most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (they get paid a percentage only if you recover). Typical contingency fees in CA run about 33%–40% (plus costs). Get the percentage in writing and ask about what expenses are deducted.
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Alameda County courts, local judges, and local medical providers helps.
- Good rapport: you should feel comfortable and respected by the attorney.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- What percentage do you charge on contingency? Are there any additional fees?
- How many similar cases have you handled? What were the outcomes?
- Do you have trial experience in Alameda County?
- Who in the firm will handle my case day-to-day?
- How will you communicate with me and how often?
- What is a realistic estimate of my case value and timeline?
- Do you advance costs (medical records, expert fees)? How are they repaid?

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report (if available)
- Photos of the scene, vehicles, injuries
- Medical records and billing statements
- Insurance information (your policy and other parties’ policies)
- Contact info for witnesses
- Any correspondence with insurers (letters, emails, recorded-statement requests)

Immediate steps you should take now
- Get prompt medical care and follow doctors’ instructions (creates medical records linking injury to accident).
- Preserve evidence: photos of damage/injuries, vehicle, skid marks; keep damaged items and clothing.
- Collect witness contact info.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the at-fault party’s insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Report the accident to your insurance company (be factual; don’t admit fault).
- Preserve vehicle repair estimates/receipts and medical bills.

Timing and deadlines (important)
- California personal-injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the date of injury to file suit. Don’t wait to consult an attorney — preserving evidence and witness memories is easier earlier.
- If your claim might be against a government entity, claim filing deadlines can be much shorter (often 6 months).

Red flags to avoid
- Pushy sales tactics or guarantees of results.
- Reluctance to put fee/terms in writing.
- Attorneys who won’t show trial experience or who delegate everything without clear supervision.
- Poor communication during your initial interactions.

If you’d like, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 personal-injury lawyers or firms near Pleasanton with relevant experience (I’ll include links and a short note on strengths), or
- Help you draft a message/email to send to attorneys to request a free consult.

Tell me how you’d like to proceed and answer the questions at the top if you want a more specific shortlist.
